planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; this is the tallest scape in Darwin's DayScape line, so give it a bit more room at the back of a mixed border.

directions: Berries and Cream carries light yellow, ruffled petals around a green throat, with a dark wine-colored eye and a matching ruffled picotee edge repeating the theme at the petal margin. It's the tallest member of the DayScape series, scaling up well for mid-border placement where the shorter DayScape cultivars would get lost. Like its siblings it starts flowering early and continues over an extended season rather than opening in one flush, and it holds up well against rust and typical daylily foliage diseases. Established clumps are low-maintenance, needing only occasional deep watering through dry stretches.

planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; one of the more compact DayScape cultivars, suited to border fronts.

directions: Coral Frill shows ruffled, coral-pink petals over a yellow throat with a dark pink eye, giving a warm two-tone effect at close range. Its low, tidy mound stays in scale at the front of a bed or along a walkway, and like the rest of the DayScape line it begins flowering early in the season and keeps producing new buds for weeks rather than finishing in a single flush. It carries good resistance to rust and general foliage disease, so it stays presentable through summer. Divide congested clumps every few years to keep bloom count high.

planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; a mid-height DayScape selection for mixed perennial beds.

directions: Golden Blaze pairs bright golden-yellow petals with a ruffled burgundy picotee edge and a matching burgundy eye, giving the flower a hot, high-contrast look from a distance. It reaches a mid-range height within the DayScape series, making it a good filler between the lowest front-of-border cultivars and taller landscape daylilies. Flowering starts early and continues steadily across the season, with spent blooms dropping cleanly, and the plant resists rust and common leaf disease well. Keep soil evenly moist through bloom for the heaviest flower count.

planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; one of the taller DayScape cultivars, good for mid-to-back border placement.

directions: Golden Yellow is the solid-color member of the DayScape series, producing uniformly golden-yellow, ruffled-edged flowers without a contrasting eye or picotee band. That simplicity makes it an easy mixer alongside more patterned daylilies and other perennials in a sunny bed. It shares the series' trait of early, continuous rebloom rather than a single flowering flush, plus solid resistance to rust and foliage disease. Water deeply during dry spells and divide crowded clumps every few years to maintain vigor.

planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; one of the shortest DayScape cultivars, well suited to edging.

directions: Lemon Meringue opens soft, light-yellow ruffled petals around a pale green throat, a gentle pastel look compared to the brighter colors elsewhere in the DayScape line. It's one of the most compact cultivars in the series, staying tidy enough for the front of a sunny bed or a container planting. Flowering begins early and carries on steadily through the season rather than stopping after one burst, and the foliage holds up well against rust and typical leaf spotting. A light deadheading of spent blooms keeps the clump looking neat.

planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; a taller DayScape cultivar suited to mid-border plantings.

directions: Peach Flame's ruffled petals are a soft apricot shade set off by a green throat and a striking violet-blue eye, an unusual color combination within the daylily world. It grows taller than most of its DayScape siblings, making it a good choice for the middle of a perennial border where it can be seen above shorter companions. The series' signature early and continuous bloom habit holds here too, along with solid resistance to rust and common foliage disease. Give it consistent moisture during the heat of summer to keep the bud count high.

planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; a mid-to-tall DayScape cultivar for a sunny perennial bed.

directions: Scarlet Burst delivers deep red, ruffled petals edged in a thin white line around a yellow eye, a crisp combination that reads well from across a garden. It sits in the taller half of the DayScape series, so give it companions that can hold their own visually rather than crowding it with short groundcovers. Blooming starts early and continues over many weeks instead of concentrating into one flush, and the plant shows good resistance to rust and foliage disease common in older daylily cultivars. An occasional deep soak during dry weather keeps the clump flowering well.

planting.note: Set out plugs or divisions in spring in average garden soil; a mid-to-tall DayScape cultivar for sunny mixed borders.

directions: Scarlet Ribbon carries deep red, ruffled petals over a yellow-green throat, a simpler color pattern than some DayScape siblings but still bold against green foliage. It reaches a similar height to the other mid-size cultivars in the series and pairs well with ornamental grasses or later-blooming perennials. The plant begins flowering early in the season and keeps producing new buds steadily rather than finishing in one quick flush, and it resists rust and typical daylily leaf disease. Established clumps need little beyond periodic deep watering in dry weather.
